minutes.headline: Select Board approved an ambulance abatement and hardship policy, heard a clean FY21 audit, and set FY23 goals.
minutes.summary: The board heard the FY21 audit from the auditors (unmodified opinion, four management letter comments), then approved a new ambulance receivable write-off and hardship policy. It reappointed members to commissions, took the town manager's report, and held a workshop reviewing FY22 goals and drafting FY23 board and town manager goals. The liquor license application policy was deferred for a draft.

budget_items.what_was_said: Auditors reported the general fund balance, its restricted and assigned parts, and the unassigned share of the budget.
General, zoning and vehicle/equipment stabilization balances reported, with general stabilization rising since 2013.

Sewer, solid waste and cable funds all grew their balances.

Worcester Regional retirement system liability and funding level reported.
Capital asset additions and outstanding debt reported; debt service about nine percent of appropriations.
Town spent federal funds subject to single audit, including COVID relief and school lunch.
Most of the ambulance receivable balance was over 180 days old, prompting the write-off policy.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a new ambulance receivable write-off and hardship policy by voice vote, as presented by the finance director and fire chief.
The auditors reported on the FY21 audit: an unmodified opinion and four management letter comments.
Auditors noted most of the ambulance receivable balance was over 180 days old, which prompted the write-off policy.
In a goals workshop, the board agreed to drop the volunteerism goal, continue the senior tax exemption goal, and carry 30 School Street into FY23.
A liquor license application review policy was held back to be drafted with legal help before the board acts.

why_it_matters: The ambulance policy sets how overdue ambulance bills are collected, written off or eased for residents in hardship, which affects what the town expects to collect.
The FY23 goals set the board's priorities, including the senior tax exemption and the 30 School Street site, which could reach residents as tax relief or a Town Meeting vote.
watch_next: A draft liquor license application review policy, to be prepared with legal help before the board acts.
The new council on aging appointee, who is to appear before the board next week to reaffirm the appointment.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the three non-procedural votes' outcomes and most audit figures, but differ on the APDC appointment vote count and on the goals decisions. The one thing to know: the official minutes record the McGrath appointment as 3-1 with Jeffreys opposed, while ours records a voice vote with no dissent.
